_about: Failure rates for the in-flight failure model and the priors of the flown-failure replicas. Every number has its source. 'opened' means the number was read in the source itself; 'excerpt' means it was read in a quoted passage of it. Rates that are not published are marked 'game' and say how they were set.

weibull_subsystems._about: On-orbit reliability of 1,584 Earth-orbiting spacecraft launched Jan 1990 to Oct 2008 (SpaceTrak), 98 total-loss failures. R(t) = exp(-(t/theta)^beta), t in years from launch. Maximum-likelihood fits of Castet and Saleh (2009, RESS 94(11):1718-1728), as tabled in J.-F. Castet, PhD thesis, Georgia Tech 2012, Table 2.3 p.33 (hdl.handle.net/1853/45871). Opened. These are fleet rates of satellites that mostly fly redundant units already, so per string they are a lower bound.

avionics_string.law: weibull per unit, a string fails when any unit fails
avionics_string.flown: MSL RCE-A NAND flash fault on sol 200, swap to RCE-B within 16 h (NASA LLIS 11201)

rcs_leak._leak: game: a fail-open valve drains 0.1% of the element's RCS load per second until isolated
rcs_leak.flown: Shuttle primary RCS: about 1.5 thruster fail-leak or fail-off per flight in the early 1990s, 38 primary thrusters (Saulsberry and McCartney 1993, NTRS 19950009917, excerpt)

battery.flown: Li-ion cell thermal runaway about 1 in 10 million cells for experienced makers (Delafuente, NASA JSC, NTRS 20200003008, opened)

isru_plant.law: weibull, from the sol the plant starts
isru_plant.flown: MOXIE on Perseverance: 16 runs, 122 g O2, no failures (NASA, Sep 6 2023; Hecht et al. 2024). Too few hours to set a rate on its own.

landing_radar._p: Posterior mean (4 + 0.5) / (34 + 1) over every radar- or lidar-guided powered landing with a published outcome and a sensor record, in data/failures/landing_sensors.json: Apollo 11 to 17, Surveyor, Chang'e-3 to 6, Chandrayaan-3, SLIM, the commercial lunar landers and 11 Mars landers. Sensor failures (class a, 4): Apollo 14 (no lock for 400 s, crew recovered), Surveyor 3 (lost lock at 37 ft), IM-2 Athena (laser altimeter noise), ispace Resilience (no valid measurements in time). Not counted as sensor failures: IM-1 (rangefinders never enabled, an integration error; class b) and HAKUTO-R M1 (software rejected good data; class c), both still counted as demands. Left out: 11 landings with no sensor record (8 Luna, Surveyor 4, Chandrayaan-2, Mars Polar Lander). Other fits on the same record: loss-causing failures only (Resilience, IM-2) 0.071; Mars only (0 in 11) 0.042; with about 600 Falcon 9 landings added as demands with no sensor failure 0.0071, but no public source confirms Falcon 9 lands on a radar altimeter, so they are not in the fit.
landing_radar.flown: Phoenix: in Dec 2006 a simulation showed the radar could lock on the falling heat shield; fixed by a 40 s later power-on (NTRS 20080034655, excerpt)

separation._p_event: Chang, Crosslink Winter 2000/2001 (Aerospace Corp), 1980-1999 world: 11 separation failures in 2,091 launches (opened). 0.53% per launch over about 3 separation events per launch (two stagings and a fairing).
separation._initiation_share: Bement, Pyrotechnic System Failures (NTRS 19880017010, excerpt): of 84 pyro system failures over 23 years, 30 initiation and 8 firing circuit (38, 45%), 32 mechanism and 14 separation (46). A second initiator covers the initiation share only.
separation.flown: NASA standard initiators: none failed in flight; 135 Shuttle flights fired 102 each (Hinkel, NTRS 20150002925, excerpt). Taurus XL OCO (2009) and Glory (2011): fairing did not separate.

launch_failure_causes._about: Chang, Space Launch Vehicle Reliability, Crosslink Winter 2000/2001, Aerospace Corp, tables for 1980-1999 (web.archive.org/web/2002/http://www.aero.org/publications/crosslink/winter2001/03.html). Opened.

new_vehicle._about: FAA/AST, Guide to Probability of Failure Analysis for New Expendable Launch Vehicles (Nov 2005), pp.4-7. Worldwide 1980-2002: experienced developers lost 5 of 18 first flights, first-time developers 8 of 11. Opened.

latent_flaw_prior._about: Prior chance that a new, untested vehicle carries a flaw of each class: the FAA first-flight loss rate of experienced developers (5/18) times the class's share of launch failures in Chang 1980-1999. Avionics (11/114) is split evenly between integration errors (polarity, wiring, assembly) and software, since Chang counts guidance software failures such as Ariane 501 as avionics.

redundancy._about: Mass of redundancy. A second avionics string is an identical copy of the first (MSL and Mars 2020 fly identical RCE-A and RCE-B; Toupet, AAS 2020, excerpt), so it doubles data.AVIONICS_PER_ELEMENT_KG. It is a cold spare and draws no power until switched in. The other masses are game estimates, marked.
redundancy._cross_strap: game: cross-strap harness and switching, 10% of one 60 kg string
redundancy._rcs_branch: game: two latching isolation valves and the branch line
redundancy._landing_radar: game: one more radar electronics box and antenna
redundancy._pyro: game: a second initiator and firing circuit per separation plane
redundancy._battery: game: a battery split into strings carries 5% more for the string switches and harness
